quests.question: My sister is funny ___ kind.
quests.hint: Two positive qualities are being listed for the same person.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two adjectives describing the same noun. The sister has both qualities.

quests.question: It was raining, ___ we stayed inside.
quests.hint: Staying inside was the direct result of the rain.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result. The rain caused them to stay inside — it is the consequence of the weather.

quests.question: He missed the bus ___ he overslept.
quests.hint: What is the reason he missed the bus?
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the direct cause of missing the bus. Oversleeping is why it happened.

quests.question: Do you want milk ___ orange juice?
quests.hint: The question offers a choice between two drinks.
quests.explanation: 'Or' presents two alternatives. In a question, it asks the listener to choose one.

quests.question: The food was cold, ___ we ate it anyway.
quests.hint: Despite the cold food, they still ate — that's unexpected.
quests.explanation: 'But' shows contrast. The food being cold would normally stop someone eating, but they ate it regardless.

quests.question: I was listening to music ___ she called me.
quests.hint: The phone call interrupted an ongoing activity.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the time point at which one event (the call) interrupted another ongoing event (listening to music).

quests.question: He is old ___ very energetic.
quests.hint: Being old and energetic is a surprising combination.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' is a coordinating conjunction showing unexpected contrast. Being old and energetic at the same time is surprising.

quests.question: You can borrow my book ___ you return it tomorrow.
quests.hint: Returning the book is a condition for borrowing it.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a condition. The borrowing is allowed only if the condition (returning tomorrow) is met.

quests.question: Wash your hands ___ you eat dinner.
quests.hint: The hand-washing should happen first, then eating follows.
quests.explanation: 'Before' is a subordinating conjunction of time. It specifies that one action (washing hands) must occur earlier than another (eating dinner).

quests.question: She reads a book ___ she waits for the bus.
quests.hint: Two activities are happening at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' is a subordinating conjunction expressing two simultaneous actions. Reading and waiting for the bus happen at the same time.

quests.question: I won't give up ___ I find a solution.
quests.hint: Not giving up continues right up to a specific moment.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the end point of an ongoing state. The refusal to give up continues until the moment a solution is found.

quests.question: We went for a walk ___ we had dinner.
quests.hint: The walk came second — dinner happened first.
quests.explanation: 'After' is a subordinating conjunction of time. It tells us the walk happened later than dinner.

quests.question: I haven't felt well ___ I caught a cold.
quests.hint: The cold is both the time point and the reason for not feeling well.
quests.explanation: 'Since' here works as both a time marker (from that point until now) and a causal conjunction (because of it). Either reading supports 'since' as the answer.

quests.question: ___ she was tired, she kept on working.
quests.hint: Being tired didn't stop her — she continued anyway.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession at the start of the sentence. Despite being tired, she continued working.

quests.question: The traffic was heavy, ___ we arrived late.
quests.hint: Heavy traffic caused a direct result — what was it?
quests.explanation: 'So' shows that the late arrival was a consequence of the heavy traffic.

quests.question: She smiled ___ she saw her old friend.
quests.hint: Seeing the friend triggered the smiling.
quests.explanation: 'When' links the smile to the specific moment she saw her friend. The sight of the friend caused the smile.

quests.question: He wore a warm coat ___ it was very cold outside.
quests.hint: What reason led him to wear a coat?
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains why he wore the coat. The cold weather is the direct reason for his choice.

quests.question: Turn off the lights ___ you go to sleep.
quests.hint: Turning off the lights should happen first.
quests.explanation: 'Before' specifies that the lights must be turned off earlier than going to sleep. It sets a time sequence.

quests.question: Either you apologise ___ we can't be friends.
quests.hint: 'Either' always pairs with one specific word when presenting a consequence.
quests.explanation: The correlative pair 'either...or' presents two outcomes. If you don't apologise, the friendship ends.

quests.question: Neither the coffee ___ the tea was hot.
quests.hint: Both hot drinks fail to meet the expectation — both are excluded.
quests.explanation: 'Neither...nor' excludes both items. Neither drink was hot — both were cold or lukewarm.

quests.question: I enjoy cooking ___ gardening in my free time.
quests.hint: Both activities are listed as things the speaker likes.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two leisure activities the speaker enjoys, indicating they like both.

quests.question: Not only did he lie, ___ he also cheated.
quests.hint: 'Not only' always pairs with one specific word to add a shocking extra point.
quests.explanation: The correlative pair 'not only...but (also)' emphasises that lying is not enough — cheating is an additional negative action.

quests.question: Both the teacher ___ the students enjoyed the lesson.
quests.hint: 'Both' always pairs with one specific word when including two parties.
quests.explanation: 'Both...and' shows that two different people/groups share the same experience. The teacher and students all enjoyed it.

quests.question: She cried ___ the film was so moving.
quests.hint: What caused her to cry?
quests.explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason for crying. The emotional power of the film is the direct cause.

quests.question: You can stay up late ___ you get up on time tomorrow.
quests.hint: There is a condition attached to staying up late.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' means 'on the condition that'. Staying up late is allowed only if waking up on time is guaranteed.

quests.question: ___ he was cooking, she set the table.
quests.hint: Both people were doing different tasks at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' introduces a simultaneous action. He cooked at the same time she set the table.

quests.question: I won't change my mind ___ you give me a very good reason.
quests.hint: Think: 'if NOT' — a good reason is the only thing that would change the mind.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'. The mind won't change except in the one case where a good reason is provided.

quests.question: I'll tell you ___ I have more information.
quests.hint: The telling will happen at a specific future moment.
quests.explanation: 'When' introduces a future time clause — the information will be shared at the moment it becomes available.

quests.question: She wasn't hungry, ___ she didn't eat much.
quests.hint: Not being hungry led directly to not eating much.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result. The lack of appetite caused her to eat very little.

quests.question: ___ it was very hot, they played football outside.
quests.hint: Playing in extreme heat seems surprising — what joins these two facts?
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession. Playing football in very hot weather is unexpected, but they did it anyway.
